A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FRACAL and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original FRACAL benchmark results, component and hyperparameter ablations, and appendix experiments comparing fractal-dimension variants.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds detection-error, confidence-calibration, spatial-distribution, and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: The main FRACAL calibration and binary extension remain unchanged. However, the optional Info and SmoothInfo variants normalize counts by G squared instead of G in appendix Equations 16–17. This changes the described variants; the PDFs do not establish an implementation change or rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate object detection and instance segmentation on LVISv1, COCO, V3Det, and OpenImages. The added appendix diagnostics analyze retained LVIS coverage without introducing another dataset, task, or input scenario.

E2.justification: V2 adds uncalibrated MaskRCNN baseline rows to the LVIS comparison in Table 2 and a Normalised Layer comparator to the V3Det comparison in Table 7, formerly Table 5b. Existing named competitors are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds COCO mask and box AP50 metrics and introduces TIDE and LaECE0/LaACE0 evaluation protocols. The new visual analysis specifies a 64-by-64 grid, a 0.01 detection threshold, and distance from the image center; confidence calibration specifies 25 bins. Existing benchmark splits and stated training budgets remain.

E4.justification: New Sections 9–11 substantially extend the analyses: Table 10 decomposes detection errors, Table 11 tests confidence calibration, and Figures 7–8 examine detected fractal dimensions, spatial spread, and five class-specific examples. Existing component, parameter, grid, inverse-weighting, and fractal-variant ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for experimental results. The added confidence-calibration metrics assess detector confidence rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Existing main AP scores are retained, but substantial diagnostic results are added. V2 Table 10 reports misclassification AP loss of 31.76 for the baseline and 16.91 for joint calibration; Table 11 reports LaECE0 of 16.8 versus 14.9 and LaACE0 of 19.8 versus 15.1. Additional results cover AP50, baselines, spatial behavior, and computation. Table 2 also introduces an erroneous +1.5 annotation for 24.5 minus 22.9.

T1.justification: Appendix B becomes Section 7 and changes the mathematical normalization in both fractal-variant definitions, Equations 16–17, from G to G squared, including the accompanying probability description. The Bayesian calibration derivation and main assumptions are retained; other equation rewrites are equivalent.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: spatially informed fractal calibration without additional training, compatibility with multiple detectors, LVIS superiority, up to 8.6% relative rare-class improvement, and generalization to the same additional datasets.

C2.justification: The spatial mechanism interpretation changes substantially: v1 describes enforcing center bias for frequent classes, whereas v2 describes greater spatial uniformity for both frequent and rare classes, including a revised reading of Figure 5. V2 also adds interpretations of classification/background-error tradeoffs and explicitly distinguishes logit adjustment from confidence calibration.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the promised code release with a specified repository link, explains storage of precomputed weights, and explicitly extends the stated Swin training setup to Swin-S. Section 12 newly reports 28 seconds of precomputation on 24 CPU cores and 90 minutes of inference using four V100 GPUs.

R1.justification: V2 adds TIDE and confidence-calibration references, including Guo and Kuzucu, and positions FRACAL relative to confidence calibration in Section 10. Equation 2 gains explicit attribution to GOL. The MMDetection reference is removed, although the framework remains named; the main related-work positioning is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: V2 selectively rewrites the methodology overview, spatial explanations, and qualitative discussion while retaining the main section sequence and much of the wording. It renames Invert FRACAL to FRACAL-Opposite, updates author information, adds acknowledgments, and renumbers the appendices.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column to a two-column layout, with revised schematics and extensive exhibit relocation. Combined benchmark tables become separate tables, Table 2 gains reference and improvement annotations, and ablation captions are corrected. New Tables 10–11 and Figures 7–8 add diagnostic displays.

improvement.justification: The new error and confidence-calibration analyses, spatial examples, computational measurements, and code-access information make the retained findings easier to assess. These benefits support a limited overall improvement. Unexplained changes to the optional-variant formulas alongside unchanged variant scores, plus small new arithmetic errors such as Table 2's +1.5 annotation, limit the gain.
